\end{enumerate}

\subsection{Uniform quantifiers and the error convention}

For the formal comparison, a one-variable polynomial error means a function
$h:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ for which there are $K\geq1$ and $r>0$ such that
$0\leq h(x)\leq Kx^r$ for every $x\geq0$. A two-variable polynomial error
means a function $g:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R$ with
\[
 \exists K\geq1\ \exists r,s>0\ \forall x,y\geq0,\qquad
 0\leq g(x,y)\leq K(x^r+y^s).
\]
This is the corrected \emph{sum} convention on the closed nonnegative
quadrant. The source shorthand instead bounds a power of the product on
positive inputs. Its replacement, including the separate one-variable
prefactor/exponent convention, is a distinct deviation; none of the
conclusions of this note resolves that issue.%
\footnote{The predicates are \path{IsPolyErr} and
\path{IsPolyErr}\textsubscript{2} in
\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Games/ErrorFunctions.lean}. The source shorthand is
\path{references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex}:19--29. Its separate notes
are \path{docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_pasting-product-error.tex} and
\path{docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_polynomial-error-square-root.tex}.}

With that convention, the proved auxiliary first chooses a point-error
function $\delta_Q$, a constant $C>0$, and a two-variable error function $g$.
Uniformly for every admissible $(q,m,d)$, real $\eps$, and projective strategy
of value at least $1-\eps$, it then constructs a complete projective joint
point family satisfying the self-consistency and both ordered-product
comparisons with error $\delta_Q(\eps)$. Relative to that same family it
constructs complete line POVMs with zero effect for axis-line outcomes above
degree $d$, and both opposite-placement consistency defects bounded by
\[
 C m\,g(\eps,md/q).
\]
The functions and all their constants precede the parameters and the strategy.
In particular, they cannot depend on $m$ or on a subsequently supplied point
family.%
\footnote{The theorem is
\path{exists_extendedLinesWitness_established} in
\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Apply.lean}; its line data are
\path{ExtendedLinesWitness} in
\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Witnesses.lean}.}

The unasserted proposition has the same existential point-family order, but
asks instead for the bound $g(m^2\eps,md/q)$ on the \emph{same direct carrier}.
It is not a theorem and does not state the original source carrier or
field-valued evaluation semantics. The conditional proved auxiliary fixes
$\delta_Q$ with its polynomial control first, then chooses $C,g$, and only
then accepts a point family at error $\delta_Q(\eps)$. It does not quantify
over arbitrary point errors independently of $\eps$.%
\footnote{The unasserted definition is
\path{PrintedExtendedLinesWitnessClaim}; the conditional theorem is
\path{exists_extendedLinesWitness_established_ofPointsWitness}, both in
\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Apply.lean}.}

\subsection{The direct carrier, law, and completed evaluations}

Put $M=2m+2$. A direct line description stores its kind, a canonical base
$b\in\F_q^M$, and an index $i\in\{0,\ldots,M-1\}$. An axis description has
direction $e_i$. A diagonal description additionally stores a direction $v$
whose coordinates below $i$ vanish; $v=0$ is allowed. The line-point law
chooses the kind with equal probabilities, and chooses a point $u$, an index
$i$, and an unrestricted direction independently and uniformly. It
canonicalizes the line through $u$, using $e_i$ in the axis case and zeroing
the direction coordinates below $i$ in the diagonal case. The sampled point
remains $u$.%
\footnote{These are \path{DirectLineDesc}, \path{DirectLdSpace}, and
\path{directLinePointDist} at \path{AdmissibleParams.extendedDirectLd}, in
\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/DirectLowDegree/Geometry.lean}.}
This directly sampled index replaces the source's field seed $s$ and
$\chi(s)$. The source seed construction at dimension $M$ requires $M\mid q$,
which admissibility does not imply, for example at $(q,m,d)=(8,2,1)$.
The direct construction is defined without that extra assumption. Its
relation to the source law is a separate question, not an identification
established by the error bound.%
\footnote{See \path{eq:chi-func} and \path{def:line-point-dist} in
\path{references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex}:207--286
and \path{docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex}.}

The line outcome is a coefficient list for a polynomial $p(T)$ of degree
at most $md+1$. At a point $u$ of the line it has value $a$ only if
$p(t)=a$ for \emph{every} parameter satisfying $u=b+tv$.
If no such $a$ exists, evaluation returns the extra answer $\bot$.
On a nonzero direction the parameter is unique. On a zero direction all
parameters represent the same point, so a coefficient polynomial that is
not constant as a function on $\F_q$ has no value there. For example,
$p(T)=T$ on a singleton evaluates to $\bot$.
Postprocessing to $\F_q\cup\{\bot\}$ retains completeness without assigning
an arbitrary field value. The joint point answer $(a,b)$ is sent to
$\alpha a+\beta b\in\F_q$, and its $\bot$ effect is zero. The two comparisons
are line on $\mathsf{AA}'$ against point on $\mathsf{BA}''$, and line on
$\mathsf{BB}'$ against point on $\mathsf{AB}''$.%
\footnote{See \path{DirectDegPoly}, \path{DirectEvaluatesTo}, and
\path{directEvalOpt} in
\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/DirectLowDegree/Game.lean}, and the two
consistency fields of \path{ExtendedLinesWitness}. The fixed scalar-field
equivalence is applied to field answers when these measurements are compared.}
These are complete measurements on the enlarged alphabet. Removing $\bot$
from the line measurement need not leave a field-valued POVM. Thus even a
proof of the unasserted direct-carrier proposition would not by itself
establish the source lemma, which uses polynomial functions on lines and
sums over $a\in\F_q$.

\section{The domain of the conditional Lean helper}

The source statement does not take an arbitrary joint point measurement as an
input.  It uses the family $\{\hat Q^{x,z}_{a,b}\}$ constructed by the preceding
point lemma, whose error has the form $\delta_Q(\eps)=\poly(\eps)$.  Consequently,
an internal theorem which accepts an already constructed point witness must retain
the same quantitative dependency: it should first fix a function
$\delta_Q:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ satisfying the one-variable polynomial-error
predicate, then choose $\delta_P$, and at strategy error $\eps$ accept only a
point witness with bound $\delta_Q(\eps)$.

Before the repair tracked by \ghissue{389}, the Lean helper
\path{exists_combinedLinesWitness_ofPointsWitness} instead had the quantifier
order
\[
 \begin{gathered}
  \exists\delta_P=\poly(\eps,md/q)\quad
  \forall\eps\ \forall\delta_Q\ \forall Q,\\
  Q\text{ has point error at most }\delta_Q\\
  \Longrightarrow T\text{ has line error at most }\delta_P(\eps,md/q).
 \end{gathered}
\]
Thus the line-error function was chosen before an unrestricted scalar
$\delta_Q$, and did not depend on it.  The fields of
\path{CombinedPointsWitness} bound self-consistency and the two ordered-product
comparisons by precisely this scalar; they impose no relation between an
arbitrary $\delta_Q$ and $\eps$.  The conditioned-pasting estimate therefore

joint point measurement deterministically, with X answer $x^{d+1}$ and a fixed
Z answer, identically on the two player sides.  Its self-consistency defect is
zero, while the two ordered-product defects are finite and hence can be covered
by a sufficiently large scalar $\delta_Q$, which the old helper quantified
arbitrarily.  On an axis X line, however, every outcome allowed by
\path{CombinedLinesWitness.axis_degree_X} evaluates as a polynomial of degree at
most $d$.  Its difference from $x^{d+1}$ has at most $d+1$ roots, so even after
mixing line outcomes the disagreement probability on that line is at least
$1-(d+1)/q$.  Since axis lines have fixed positive weight in the line-point
law, the resulting line consistency defect stays bounded away from zero as
$q\to\infty$.  In contrast, the two-variable polynomial-error predicate forces
$\delta_P(0,d/q)\to0$.  This argument diagnoses the theorem interface; no Lean
counterexample theorem is asserted here.

\[
 \begin{gathered}
  \forall\delta_Q,\quad \delta_Q=\poly(\eps)\Longrightarrow
  \exists\delta_P=\poly(\eps,md/q),\\
  \forall\eps\ \forall Q\text{ with error }\delta_Q(\eps),\\
  \exists T\text{ with error }\delta_P(\eps,md/q).

declaration \path{exists_combinedLinesWitness} preserves its original statement:
it existentially obtains $\delta_Q$ and its point witnesses from the preceding
point construction, then applies the conditional helper.

\path{combined_line_measurement_consistency}. For a joint point family
with error $\delta_Q(\eps)=\poly(\eps)$, it proves evaluated consistency
of the explicit unconditioned measurement

 T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}
 =L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X)L^Z_{f_Z}(\ell_Z)L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X)
\]
under the original product of line-point distributions, with polynomial error

placement. The point-to-line comparisons at source lines 900--941 and the
pasting argument at lines 942--961 supply the proof. The POVM,
axis-degree properties, and X marginal of this same measurement are proved.

measurement unchanged. On this event, the polynomial root bound gives the
conditional collision estimate needed for pasting. Multiplication by the
retained probability and addition of the discarded contribution, at most

statement. The current heterogeneous pasting theorem requires only the two

Issue [#667](https://github.com/Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A/issues/667) fixes the
source snapshot at `e947a49e14080b46642be21ce551d911032a05f4`. All 21 QPBT
notes were inventoried and their assertions compared with the cited mirrors,
blueprint entries, and current Lean carriers. The two rows immediately above
were absent from the earlier register. The inventory now records six
`no-difference` rows, four `corrected` rows, six `open` rows, and five `pending`
rows. The audit itself adopted no mathematical correction or exemption; main
later adopted only the cross-basis phase and decoder corrections after the
independent review cited in their rows below.

The four adoption conditions are correctness, sufficiency for every source and
blueprint consumer, minimality, and Lean convergence
(development protocol `local/protocols/issues-prs.md`, section 6, not included
in the artifact). A proved
replacement and a successful final theorem do not by themselves certify an
unproved printed assertion. In particular, C3 does not permit replacing a
conclusion by a weaker one merely because the weaker conclusion suffices later.
For a well-formed printed claim that is not proved, its required unasserted
Lean record is an additional artifact, not a proof. The two index corrections
below repair ill-typed expressions; there is no well-formed universal proposition
with the original dependent indices to retain as a separate theorem claim.

and marked blueprint consumers were loaded in the successful 1,842-declaration
axiom audit (368 modules), and that all 2,116 blueprint declaration names resolved.
It does not certify equality with the paper, the unmarked source statements, or
an independent review. The five `pending` rows explicitly identify the adoption
checks left uncertified; no other row is silently treated as checked.

The source and formal recursive definitions of CL functions agree: each tree
node chooses a register and a supported linear map, and its remainder is
supported on the complementary register. Restriction-invariance supplies the
source input to the remainder. Extending unused branches outside the first
map's image by zero changes no value. `IsTypedCondLinearFamily` applies this
predicate pointwise; its finite-index specialization is the source definition.

uniform seed, with the typed version first sampling the graph law. Defining
the same sampling formula on arbitrary maps does not add a hypothesis or alter
its restriction to CL maps.

+canonicalizes the line through $u$, using $e_i$ in the axis case and zeroing
+the direction coordinates below $i$ in the diagonal case. The sampled point
+remains $u$.%

+The line outcome is a coefficient list for a polynomial $p(T)$ of degree
+at most $md+1$. At a point $u$ of the line it has value $a$ only if

+On a nonzero direction the parameter is unique. On a zero direction all
+parameters represent the same point, so a coefficient polynomial that is
+not constant as a function on $\F_q$ has no value there. For example,
+$p(T)=T$ on a singleton evaluates to $\bot$.
+Postprocessing to $\F_q\cup\{\bot\}$ retains completeness without assigning
+an arbitrary field value. The joint point answer $(a,b)$ is sent to
+$\alpha a+\beta b\in\F_q$, and its $\bot$ effect is zero. The two comparisons

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Merge approved URL normalization and independent whole register-row edits."""
from pathlib import Path
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

root = Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve()
def git(*args):
    return subprocess.check_output(['git', '-C', str(root), *args])

def independent_register_rows(content):
    """Choose a changed whole row only when the other side equals its base."""
    conflict = re.compile(
        rb'^<<<<<<< [^\n]*\n(.*?)^\|\|\|\|\|\|\| [^\n]*\n(.*?)^=======\n(.*?)^>>>>>>> [^\n]*\n',
        re.MULTILINE | re.DOTALL)
    key_pattern = re.compile(rb'^\| (\[`qpbt_[^`]+\.tex`\]\([^)]+\)) \|')
    def resolve(match):
        sides = [section.splitlines(keepends=True) for section in match.groups()]
        keys = []
        for lines in sides:
            matches = [key_pattern.match(line) for line in lines]
            assert lines and all(matches), 'Conflict includes non-register-row prose'
            identifiers = [item.group(1) for item in matches]
            assert len(set(identifiers)) == len(identifiers), 'Duplicate row identity'
            keys.append(identifiers)
        assert keys[0] == keys[1] == keys[2], 'Register rows added, removed or reordered'
        merged = []
        for ours, base, theirs in zip(*sides):
            if ours == base:
                merged.append(theirs)
            elif theirs == base or ours == theirs:
                merged.append(ours)
            else:
                raise AssertionError('Both branches changed the same register row')
        return b''.join(merged)
    result, count = conflict.subn(resolve, content)
    assert count and not re.search(rb'^(<<<<<<<|\|\|\|\|\|\|\||>>>>>>>)( |$)', result, re.MULTILINE)
    return result

assert git('rev-parse', '--show-toplevel').decode().strip() == str(root)
git('rev-parse', '--verify', 'MERGE_HEAD')
paths = [p.decode() for p in git('diff', '--name-only', '--diff-filter=U', '-z').split(b'\0') if p]
assert paths, 'No unresolved merge to normalize'
old = b'https://github.com/Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A/'
new = b'https://github.com/Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-QPBT/'
resolved = {}
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='qpbt-reviewed-url-merge-') as temp:
    scratch = Path(temp)
    for index, path in enumerate(paths):
        relative = Path(path)
        assert relative.parts[0] in ('docs', 'blueprint') and relative.suffix in ('.md', '.tex'), path
        assert '..' not in relative.parts and not (root / path).is_symlink(), path
        base, ours, theirs = (git('show', f':{stage}:{path}') for stage in (1, 2, 3))
        assert any(old in content for content in (base, ours, theirs)), f'{path}: no approved URL overlap'
        inputs = []
        for name, content in (('ours', ours), ('base', base), ('theirs', theirs)):
            target = scratch / f'{index}-{name}'
            target.write_bytes(content.replace(old, new))
            inputs.append(str(target))
        result = subprocess.run(['git', 'merge-file', '-p', '--diff3', *inputs], capture_output=True)
        if 0 < result.returncode < 128 and path == 'docs/paper-gaps/qpbt-gap-register.md':
            content = independent_register_rows(result.stdout)
        else:
            assert result.returncode == 0, f'{path}: substantive conflict remains; no conflict file rewritten'
            content = result.stdout
        assert old not in content, f'{path}: old URL remains'
        resolved[path] = content

# Publish no partial resolution if another path fails either equality guard.
for path, content in resolved.items():
    (root / path).write_bytes(content)
git('add', '--', *resolved)
assert not git('diff', '--name-only', '--diff-filter=U', '-z')
for path in resolved:
    print('Approved URL normalization and independent whole-row merge passed:', path)

#!/bin/sh
set -eu

ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
cd "$ROOT"
HOOK_ROOT="$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
GIT_LOCAL_ENV_VARS="$(git rev-parse --local-env-vars)"

run_without_git_local_env() (
  # Git exports repository-local variables while running hooks.  Several script
  # tests create temporary repositories; keep those tests independent of this
  # checkout.
  unset $GIT_LOCAL_ENV_VARS
  "$@"
)

# A merge commit can be syntactically valid while its index has been reset to
# the first-parent tree.  That failure mode silently discarded clean incoming
# additions on issue-109 and issue-110 (issue #222).  Check the pending index
# before every other gate, including the documented blanket hook bypass: a
# missing incoming path is valid only when the branch deleted a base path.
MERGE_HEAD_PATH="$(git rev-parse --git-path MERGE_HEAD)"
if [ -f "$MERGE_HEAD_PATH" ]; then
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: checking the merge result for silent incoming loss."
  python3 "$HOOK_ROOT/local/bin/merge_loss_guard.py" --repo "$ROOT"
fi

# Scope-control guard (EVOLUTION.md 2026-09-01, the issue-0007 overbuild):
# workflow scaffolding is budgeted at <=1000 changed lines per commit (400 until the owner raised it on 2026-09-05).  This is
# mechanical enforcement — repeated verbal correction of scaffolding bloat did
# not stick, so the budget lives in the hook.  The override env var is granted
# only after a recorded main decision, never self-granted by a worker session. Runs
# before the ACMR early-exit so deletion-only commits are counted too
# (numstat includes deletions; PR 7 round 3, F8), and before the
# MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS exit so a blanket hook skip cannot launder the
# workflow budget override.
# A merge that carries main stages already-reviewed content.  A merge head
# contained in github/main measures the budget against MERGE_HEAD; a merge head
# that contains github/main (a parent branch of a stack that already merged
# main; owner decision 2026-09-05) measures it against github/main, so inherited
# main content counts zero while the PR's cumulative workflow diff and any
# side-branch content beyond main still count.  Any other side-branch merge
# stays budgeted against HEAD.
if [ -f "$MERGE_HEAD_PATH" ] &&
    git merge-base --is-ancestor MERGE_HEAD refs/remotes/github/main 2>/dev/null; then
  BUDGET_BASE="$(git rev-parse MERGE_HEAD)"
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: main-history merge; budget measured against MERGE_HEAD."
elif [ -f "$MERGE_HEAD_PATH" ] &&
    git merge-base --is-ancestor refs/remotes/github/main MERGE_HEAD 2>/dev/null; then
  BUDGET_BASE="$(git rev-parse refs/remotes/github/main)"
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: non-main merge carrying github/main; workflow-layer content beyond github/main is budgeted."
else
  BUDGET_BASE=""
  if [ -f "$MERGE_HEAD_PATH" ]; then
    echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: non-main merge; workflow-layer merge content is budgeted."
  fi
fi
INFRA_CHANGED="$(git diff --cached --numstat $BUDGET_BASE -- local/ .githooks/ \
  scripts/tests/test_dispatch.py scripts/tests/test_github_workflow.py \
  scripts/tests/test_lake_root.py scripts/tests/test_pre_push_hook.py \
  scripts/tests/test_ready_packets.py scripts/tests/test_merge_loss_guard.py \
  | awk '{added=$1; deleted=$2; if (added != "-") total+=added+deleted} END {print total+0}')"
if [ "${INFRA_CHANGED:-0}" -gt 1000 ] && [ "${MIPSTARRE_INFRA_OVERRIDE:-}" != "1" ]; then
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: staged workflow-layer change is ${INFRA_CHANGED} lines (budget: 1000)."
  echo "Scope control (local/personas/main.md): the budget is PER EPISODE, not per"
  echo "commit — serial oversized commits are the same violation and show in the"
  echo "telemetry. Shrink the change, or stop for a recorded main decision that"
  echo "authorizes MIPSTARRE_INFRA_OVERRIDE=1; workers must not self-grant it."
  exit 1
fi

if [ "${MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS:-}" = "1" ]; then
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit hook skipped by MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS=1."
  exit 0
fi

STAGED_FILES="$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACMR)"
if [ -z "$STAGED_FILES" ]; then
  exit 0
fi

echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: checking staged whitespace."
# Paper mirrors under references/ are byte-faithful captures of external
# arXiv sources (see references/*/README.md); their inherited trailing
# whitespace is part of the fidelity claim and must not be "fixed", so they
# are exempt from the whitespace gate (local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md,
# 2026-08-30).
git diff --cached --check -- ':(exclude)references/'

if printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_FILES" | grep -Eq '^scripts/(.*\.py|tests/.*)$'; then
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: running scripts/tests unit tests."
  run_without_git_local_env python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -p 'test_*.py'
fi

if printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_FILES" | grep -Eq \
  '^(blueprint/src/.*\.(tex|sty|cls)|scripts/(check_blueprint_latex|tex_utils)\.py|scripts/tests/test_check_blueprint_latex\.py|\.githooks/pre-commit)$'; then
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: checking blueprint LaTeX conventions."
  python3 scripts/check_blueprint_latex.py --root blueprint/src
fi

if ! printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_FILES" | grep -Eq \
  '^(MIPStarRE/|MIPStarRE\.lean|blueprint/src/|blueprint/lean_decls|scripts/(audit_new_proof_obligation_metadata|audit_paper_facing_proof_debt|audit_conclusion_shaped_hypotheses|audit_unfaithful_markers|audit_lean_axiom_declarations|check_blueprint_latex|check_paper_gap_note_style|check_statement_paper_origin|check_source_statement_changes|blueprint_lean_sync|lean_header_utils|tex_utils)\.py|docs/(CONTRIBUTING|project_conventions|anti_patterns|blueprint_style_guide|formalization-patterns|proof_frontier_review)\.md|docs/paper-gaps/|\.github/(actions|prompts|workflows)/|AGENTS\.md)'; then
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: no statement-integrity files staged."
  exit 0
fi

echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: checking changed paper-gap note structure."
python3 scripts/check_paper_gap_note_style.py --root . --staged --ci

echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: checking statement-like paper-origin citations."
python3 scripts/check_statement_paper_origin.py --root .

echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: checking new proof-obligation metadata."
python3 scripts/audit_new_proof_obligation_metadata.py --root . --staged --ci

echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: checking paper-facing proof-debt headers."
echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: do not close proof gaps by adding non-paper bridge/package hypotheses."
python3 scripts/audit_paper_facing_proof_debt.py --root . --ci

echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: checking conclusion-shaped hypotheses."
python3 scripts/audit_conclusion_shaped_hypotheses.py --root . --ci

echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: checking unfaithful-dependency markers."
python3 scripts/audit_unfaithful_markers.py --root . --ci

echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: checking explicit LDT axiom declarations."
python3 scripts/audit_lean_axiom_declarations.py --root . --ci

echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: ok."

	into $m\cdot\poly(\eps,md/q)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Joint projected law of the concrete direct sub-line sampler]
\label{lem:qld-subline-joint-mixture}
\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.subLineJointProjection, MIPStarRE.QPBT.subLineDist_map_joint}
\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.avgOver_subLineJointProjection_le}
\leanok
\uses{def:ith-restricted-line, lem:restricted-line-mixture-bounds}
This is a formalization-only assertion for the directly indexed law
$D_{\mathrm{dir}}$ defined by \texttt{subLineDist}, with its concrete choices
of source indices. Choose a line kind $v$ uniformly from the two kinds and
$k$ uniformly from $\{0,\ldots,2m+1\}$. Put $i_X(k)=k$ for $k<m$ and
$i_X(k)=0$ otherwise; put $i_Z(k)=k-m$ for $m\leq k<2m$ and $i_Z(k)=0$
otherwise. Let $\mu$ be the law of $(v,i_X(k),i_Z(k))$.
Sample $(\ell,\ell_X,\ell_Z)$ from $D_{\mathrm{dir}}$ and a uniform affine
parameter $t$, and set $u=\ell(t)$. Then
\[
 \operatorname{Law}((\ell_X,u_X),(\ell_Z,u_Z))
 =\sum_{v,i,j}\mu(v,i,j)\bigl(D_{v,i}\times D_{v,j}\bigr).
\]
In particular, for every nonnegative function $F$ of two source line-point
pairs,
\[
 \mathbb{E}_{D_{\mathrm{dir}},t}F((\ell_X,u_X),(\ell_Z,u_Z))
 \leq 4m^2\mathbb{E}_{D_{\mathrm{Line}}\times D_{\mathrm{Line}}}F.
\]
Zero directions and singleton lines are included. The assertion concerns
this concrete direct law, not every distribution with the separate marginal
properties of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-sublines}.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
\leanok
For fixed $v,k$, replacing the original uniform extended point by a uniform
point of its line preserves its uniform law and both source-line
representatives. Its two coordinate blocks, the two direction blocks, and
the two source seeds then form independent restricted samples. Averaging
this joint identity over $v,k$ gives the displayed law. Apply the
nonnegative restricted-product estimate of
Lemma~\ref{lem:restricted-line-mixture-bounds} in each component.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Conditional direct sub-line consistency]
\label{rem:qld-subline-joint-consistency}
In a projective setting, suppose a point witness $Q$ and a joint line
witness $T$ are supplied, with completed-answer consistency defect at most
$\delta_P$ over two independent source line-point samples. For any directed
pair of opposite expanded placements, their completed evaluations at
$(u_X,u_Z)$, sampled from the concrete law $D_{\mathrm{dir}}$ above, have
consistency defect at most $4m^2\delta_P$.
This conditional auxiliary proves the distribution comparison used in the
second route at source lines 1241--1245. Construction of $T$ with a suitable
error, and the error form of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-13}, remain separate
obligations.

The integrand defining the completed consistency defect is nonnegative
because the two measurements act on opposite registers. Apply
Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-subline-joint-mixture} to that integrand and use the
assumed consistency bound on $T$.
\end{remark}

\begin{lemma}[Formalization support for Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-13}]
	\label{lem:qld-4-13-established}
	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_extendedLinesWitness_established}
	\leanok
	\uses{lem:qld-4-10, def:line, def:line-point-dist, def:consistency,
		def:bracket, def:expanded-state, def:ideg-deg-polynomials}
	This formalization-only auxiliary is not a named statement of the paper.
	It records a directly indexed auxiliary with the numerical error estimate
	$C \cdot m \cdot \poly(\eps, md/q)$ obtained from the first route in the
	printed proof, for a universal constant $C > 0$. It does not claim either
	the printed error form $\poly(m^2\eps, md/q)$ or the source question carrier,
	line-point law, and field-valued answer sum of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-13}; see
	Remark~\ref{rem:qld-4-13-source-defects}.
	More precisely, there exist a polynomially controlled function
	$\delta_Q:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, a constant $C>0$, and a polynomially
	controlled function
	$\delta_{\mathrm{combine}}:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R$ such that, for every admissible
	$(q,m,d)$ and every projective strategy passing with error $\eps$, there is a
	complete projective joint point family satisfying all the conclusions of
	Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-10} with error $\delta_Q(\eps)$ and, relative to that
	same point family, an extended-line witness whose axis-degree property and
	both completed-answer consistency bounds hold with error
	\[
		C m\,\delta_{\mathrm{combine}}\!\left(\eps,\frac{md}{q}\right).
	\]
	Within the directly indexed, completed-answer setting described below, the
	quantitative change from the printed estimate is the error form. Compared
	with Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-13}, the auxiliary construction also differs in
	three respects. Its extended questions are
	drawn from the directly indexed line space of
	\cite{gap:qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility} rather than from the lines of
	$\F_q^{2m+2}$ used above; its average is taken over the corresponding
	directly indexed line-point law rather than over the line-point
	distribution of Definition~\ref{def:line-point-dist} instantiated at
	dimension $2m+2$, whose definition is blocked by the divisibility
	obstruction of Remark~\ref{rem:qld-4-7-divisibility}; and both sides of
	its two consistency displays are compared on the completed answer
	alphabet $\F_q \cup \{\bot\}$, whose extra outcome collects the line
	polynomials that admit no evaluation at the sampled point, rather than
	under the answer summation over $a \in \F_q$ used above. Thus the auxiliary
	construction does not establish the source formulation until the question carrier
	and law are related by the transport obligation of
	\cite{gap:qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility} and the completed answer comparison
	is related to the source sum by
	\cite{gap:qpbt_combined-lines-error-term}.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
\leanok
\uses{lem:qld-4-10, lem:qld-4-13-established-given-points}
Construct the polynomially controlled joint point family of
Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-10}, and apply
Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-13-established-given-points} to that same family. This
proves the stated directly indexed auxiliary. Its comparison with the printed source formulation remains subject
to the separate question-law and completed-answer issues in
\cite{gap:qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility} and
\cite{gap:qpbt_combined-lines-error-term}.
\end{proof}
